what: Contextual chunk embedding was already built, and measuring it produced a null result: the heading trail is 13.7% of every embedded passage on the aveline corpus and moves no case up the ranking.

the_item_was_already_done.what_the_roadmap_asked: 'The remaining half of the contextual-retrieval idea is prepending each chunk's heading trail before embedding it - the chunker already carries the trail for a different reason.'
the_item_was_already_done.what_is_actually_there: `_passage` in retrieval/base.py writes the trail as the first line of each chunk's text, and the embedder embeds chunk.text. So the trail is already in the vector - and in the BM25 index too, which is more than the item asked for. It arrived as a side effect of the 'heading said once' change; the roadmap entry predated it and was never struck through.
the_item_was_already_done.checked_not_assumed: 68 of 68 chunks on the aveline corpus begin with their own heading trail; 67 of 68 contain the document title, because the trail's first element is the H1. Building the item as written would have prepended the trail a second time and inflated every embedded passage.

so_it_was_measured_instead.instrument: tools/measure_context.py - the rank of each labelled case's required citation, with the trail in the embedded text and with it removed.
so_it_was_measured_instead.dense_only_on_purpose: The first attempt ranked through the shipped hybrid retriever and showed all 14 cases at rank 1 both ways, which measured nothing: BM25 does not care where in a passage a word sits, and on an 11-document corpus whose questions name their subject it finds the document regardless. Ranking by cosine alone is the only way the trail's contribution is visible at all.
so_it_was_measured_instead.result: 68 chunks, 14 cases with a required citation. With the trail: median rank 1.0, mean 1.143, top-1 12/14, top-3 14/14. Trail stripped: median 1.0, mean 1.143, top-1 12/14, top-3 14/14. Zero cases better, zero worse, fourteen unchanged.
so_it_was_measured_instead.the_experiment_was_real: Checked, because a null result from a no-op experiment looks identical to a null result from a real one: all 68 chunks differ between the two variants, and 13.7% of the embedded words are the trail. Something was removed; nothing moved.

what_this_does_and_does_not_say.does_not_say_the_trail_is_worthless: Fourteen cases on sixty-eight chunks, with the required document already at rank 1 in twelve of them, cannot show an improvement - there is nowhere up to go. The corpus is the limiting factor.
what_this_does_and_does_not_say.does_say: This corpus cannot justify the 13.7%, and any future claim that the trail helps retrieval needs a corpus that can discriminate. That is the labelled real corpus the roadmap already lists, and it needs somebody's real folder.
what_this_does_and_does_not_say.and_the_trail_has_another_job: Its stated purpose in `_passage` is that a passage retrieved alone still says what it is about, which is a grounding and citation property rather than a ranking one. This measurement says nothing about that, and the golden sets already exercise it.

the_ceiling_that_shaped_this: Both golden sets sit at 100%, so they can prove a retrieval change breaks nothing and cannot show one helps. That is worth stating plainly: 'gated by the golden sets' means regression-proof, not measured-as-better. Showing improvement needs either harder cases or an instrument like this one, and this one has just demonstrated that the available corpora saturate too.
gate: No code change to retrieval, prompting, chunking or grounding - the finding is that the change was already made. tools/measure_context.py is a new measurement tool and touches nothing the product runs.
still_open: Re-run measure_context.py on a corpus large enough to discriminate. Until then the trail's 13.7% is a design decision with a stated rationale and no supporting number.
